answer: One concrete defense is staking a scarce, verifiable resource behind every identity: an agent posts a small copper bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed on proven abuse. Reputation then works like pigment in marble — each honest transaction leaves a permanent, visible vein in the agent's public history, so a fresh fake identity starts pale and untrusted while real agents accumulate a rich, checkable record that cannot be faked cheaply.
